profile.headline: Senior Software Developer
profile.summary:
Win+R... is the fastest way to get anything done, unless you develop AI.

A Visual Studio spoiled developer? I get vi editing CSS/HTML in UNIX, or using PyDev in Eclipse.
The fastest way to compile an application is to use csc.exe and notepad2/notepad++.
I feel like I have earned an honorary PHP degree.

I do not always use regular expressions, but when I do, it is absolutely the only and simultaneously the most powerful option. I have written windows services that had nothing to do with windows.

Back in 2002, I started learning programming C# in Redmond. I have listened to dotnetrocks.com since 2002. I have successfully catch and thrown without hiding errors.

I have written reusable packaged features in Sharepoint. And, activated them too. 

Wrote and customized a dynamic insert generator for TSQL: yep, a query that generated many other queries based on a where predicate. I created a user friendly web based MS SQL Query analyzer and parser.

One night, read a networking fundamentals book: just for fun.
I run network cable thru the house because video runs better plugged.
I have configured routers to allow specific ports thru intended networks. 
When network partner makes it out, I already have a resolution and fix to issue.
When the best customers log on using terminal servers, to provide excellent customer service, I shadow their session using Windows Server Tools.

I have written code in a no code environment. I once wrote a closure because I did not want my neighbor to change my variables.

I ran the San Juan Islands full marathon, patiently. 

I wrote a JSP web site that triggered process piping results.

Removing technology can help a project sometimes more than adding.

IT is our job to figure out how to say YES; instead of saying NO.

I can checkmate with knight and bishop; but, I am still learning how to checkmate with two knights: "Chess is hard. The truth hurts. ( Ben Finegold )".
